tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with 'Deep investigation of a single AWS Elemental MediaLive channel. Use when a customer reports a MediaLive problem or when evidence points at the encoding layer...' which uses imperative phrasing ('Use when'), focuses on the triggering scenario (customer-reported issues, specific symptoms) rather than implementation mechanics, lists many explicit trigger contexts (input loss, dropped frames, fill/black frames, active alerts, output 4xx/5xx errors, pipeline desync, schedule anomalies, SCTE-35), and also explicitly scopes out adjacent skills to avoid overlap. It is a dense but bounded paragraph, appropriate given the breadth of the skill's coverage.
tests.evidence: Use when a customer reports a MediaLive problem or when evidence points at the encoding layer: input loss, dropped frames, fill or black frames in output, active alerts, output 4xx/5xx push errors, pipeline desynchronization on STANDARD channels, or schedule and input-switch anomalies...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps straight into MediaLive-specific CLI commands, metric names, and non-obvious domain facts (e.g., FillMsec capping behavior, EventBridge delivery caveats) without explaining general concepts the agent would already know.
tests.evidence: "UPDATING is captured in the console but is NOT emitted via EventBridge. Do not rely on EventBridge state-change events to detect config updates in progress."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed tabular reference data (metric tables, lookup tables) has been consistently offloaded to references/lookup-tables.md and other reference files, with the body only containing short analysis blocks and pointers. The MQCS section includes some detail but it is procedural guidance (queries/order) rather than a large static reference table.
tests.evidence: "Table: [Step 3: Encoding diagnosis: Core encoding metrics (per-pipeline)](references/lookup-tables.md#step-3-encoding-diagnosis-core-encoding-metrics-per-pipeline). Load it when you run this step."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ (alert-retrieval.md, channel-health-checklist.md, encoder-log-parsing.md, input-type-patterns.md, lookup-tables.md, mqcs-metrics.md, output-destination-checks.md) has a markdown link in the body.

tests.name: Reference path format

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations like MQCS metric discovery and RECOVERING state handling get exact instructions and thresholds, while compiling findings gives the agent reasoning freedom (observed/expected/question framing) rather than rigid scripts.
tests.evidence: "Do not declare a definitive root cause; surface evidence and the precise question that follows from it."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple options exist (e.g., alert detail retrieval paths), the skill lists them in priority order as fallback paths rather than an undifferentiated menu.
